items.name: Take Tour NANTABI
items.description_ja: NANTABI｜Take Tour｜Stuffed with charm Local departure tour
items.description: NANTABI｜Take Tour｜Stuffed with charm Local departure tour
body_paragraphs: Inami, located in the city of Nanto, Toyama Prefecture, is Japan's foremost woodcarving town and a designated piece of Japan Heritage. The town is home to some 200 woodcarvers who practice traditional carving techniques passed down since the 18th century. At its center is Inami Betsuin Zuisenji, a historic temple whose every beam and column is furnished with elaborate carved decorations—a practical museum of woodcarvings. This special nighttime tour allows you to explore this one-of-a-kind space with a master woodcarver as your guide. Tours are accompanied by a dedicated guide-interpreter who will translate the carver's remarks. Inquire about an experience today.
JPY 33,000 per group up to 10 people; JPY 2,000 for each additional person(JPY 35,000 for 11 people; JPY 37,000 for 12 people, etc.; tax included)

Discover Kokiriko, the oldest folk song in Japan, and the quiet village that preserves it. Nestled between UNESCO-listed gassho-style villages, Kaminashi is a center of culture in a region whose rugged geography and unusually snowy climate once made it nearly inaccessible, a virtual “island in the mountains” whose traditions have been shaped by centuries of isolation. On your walk through the village, you’ll discover this unique heritage—the Kokiriko song and dance, Gokayama tofu, and more—as you interact firsthand with the people who keep the traditions alive.
JPY 20,000 per person (tax included)
Daily (February through November) Weekends and holidays only (December through February)

Uncover the hidden side of life in Suganuma, a gassho-style village that joined the register of UNESCO World Heritage Sites in 1995. Surrounded by rich forests and steep mountains, Suganuma is a living piece of cultural heritage–a village with permanent residents, which makes it unique among the sites on the UNESCO roster. During your journey, you’ll discover the local origins of the village’s world-famous gassho-style architecture and savor a lunch prepared using local ingredients in a traditional gassho-style home.
JPY 16,000 per person (tax included)

This is a forest path cycling tour of the Gokayama area that includes a stroll through the World Heritage Site of Ainokura Gassho-Zukuri Village.We will take you to spectacular spots that cannot be reachedby public transportation, but only by bicycle.With electric bicycles, even beginners and those who are not confident in their fitness can enjoy cycling while taking their time to enjoy the scenery.
JPY 45,000 per Group (tax included)
1-6 people (minimum: 1 people)

Gain a deeper appreciation for the beauty of Japanese tradition as you journey through Inami, a town that's practically a museum of wood sculptures. You'll visit historic Zuisenji Temple and stop by a carver's studio. You'll carve your own wooden sake cup with real tools under the guidance of a master—an experience like no other. You'll savor a fine Japanese lunch in a traditional home and tour the earthen brewhouse of the Wakakoma Sake Brewery, where you'll have a chance to sample local sake in the wooden cup you created.
JPY 26,000 per person (tax included)

A three-day, two-night tour to experience Gokayama's traditional culture, local cuisine, and hot springs. Cycle through the forest roads of Gokayama and stay at a guest house in the World Heritage Site of Ainokura Gassho-Zukuri Village. Enjoy folk songs in a room with a sunken hearth.Discover the hidden charms of Gokayama by cycling on paths that cannot be reached by public transportation.
JPY 75,000 per person (tax included)
2-6 people (minimum: 2 people)

items.name_ja: ようこそ射水
items.name: ようこそ射水
items.description_ja: 射水市がどんなまちかをご紹介。港町の風情が残る海まちエリア、歴史と文化と遊びがいっぱいの里まちエリアの特色や、海から里山までの多彩な魅力や食文化、イベント情報をまとめています。
items.description: 射水市がどんなまちかをご紹介。港町の風情が残る海まちエリア、歴史と文化と遊びがいっぱいの里まちエリアの特色や、海から里山までの多彩な魅力や食文化、イベント情報をまとめています。
body_paragraphs: 射水市公式観光サイトへようこそ！射水（いみず）市がどんなまちなのかご紹介します。
日本最古の歌集「万葉集」にも登場する「射水」という地名には、水が湧き出るという意味が込められています。県内有数の大河に挟まれ、豊かな水脈の張り巡らされた射水市には、港町の風情あるまち並みや文化が脈々と受け継がれている海まちエリア、自然豊かな公園や、旧街道沿いに広がる歴史深い里まちエリアがあります。ここにしかない、みずみずしい体験があなたを待っています。
射水市公式キャラクター。水の国で生まれた王様で、夢は射水市をきららかで幸せなまちにすること。
庄川と神通川に挟まれた射水市。東に立山連峰、西に能登半島を望む県内第3の都市です。富山湾に面し、古くから漁業や船運で栄えた港町の情緒溢れる海まちエリア、内陸側には、旧北陸街道沿いに栄えてきた歴史と文化の薫る町と、農産物や自然体験の宝庫である里まちエリアがあります。県内2大都市の間にあり交通アクセスもよく、コンパクトな地形に魅力が「ギュギュッと！」凝縮されています。
「天然のいけす」と呼ばれる富山湾。目の前に漁場のある新湊漁港は、水揚げされる魚の新鮮さ、多様な漁法による魚種の多さが自慢。全国的にも珍しい「昼セリ」も行われています。豊かな水脈と肥沃な土壌が広がる射水平野では、米や枝豆や白ネギ、梨や柿など多彩な農作物が作られています。たけのこや山菜などの山の幸も。各エリアに伝わる伝統食のほか、「イミズスタン」などの新たな食文化も生まれています。
千年あまり前から、先人たちから脈々と引き継がれてきた伝統文化。各時代の担い手たちが夢中になって取り組み、その技を極め、世界観を醸成し、まちの人々を熱狂させ続けてきた祭りが、今も各地に息づいています。県内最古かつ最多を誇る獅子舞、県内最多・総勢20基の勇壮華麗な曳山祭り、広大な敷地に2万株が咲き誇るあじさい祭りなど、一度体験したら忘れられない感動に、きっと出逢えます。
古くから漁業や交易で栄えた海まちエリアには、大伴家持が残した数々の万葉歌、鎌倉期には亡命した将軍が幕府を樹立するという数奇な歴史が。近年注目の集まる内川周辺には、今も情緒溢れる風景が広がります。 戦国の頃から街道沿いの要衝として栄えた里まちエリアには、歴史的な建物が数多く点在。江戸時代に花開いた小杉左官による芸術的な鏝絵がまちのそこここを彩っています。
海路も街道も、未知との出会いと交易にかかせない「みち」なんだ

富山県の2大都市（富山市・高岡市）の間にあり、幹線道路が整備されている射水市。海側には高岡市から延びる路面電車「万葉線」、内陸には県内を横断する「あいの風とやま鉄道」が走っています。市内主要エリア間はコミュニティバスやAIオンデマンドバス「のるーと射水」がカバーしているほか、海まちエリアの一部では電動カートなどのユニークな観光モビリティも。移動のしやすさはもちろん、移動自体も楽しいのも、射水ならではです！
射水市では季節ごとに多彩なイベントが開催され、訪れる人々を楽しませています。地域ならではの交流イベントも多く、地元の人々と触れ合えるのも魅力です。
海まちエリアの新湊大橋や内川沿いの町並みなど、射水ならではの絶景や風情ある景観が楽しめます。観光船で水辺のまちを巡れば、非日常感たっぷりの体験に。歴史文化に触れられる寺社や資料館もあり、街歩き好きにもおすすめです。
新鮮な海鮮グルメはもちろん、地元で親しまれてきたローカルグルメまで、射水ならではの多彩なおいしさに出会えます。さらに、海産加工品や地元農産物、スイーツなどおみやげもいっぱい！知る人ぞ知るお店でしか手に入らないアイテムもあるんです。
射水市を愛する地元のボランティアガイドたちが、射水旅の思い出づくりのお手伝いをいたします！

items.description_ja: 射水市ならではのユニークな魅力をテーマ別にまとめた特集ページです。海まちエリアや里まちエリア、おまつり、お土産・グルメ、歴史・文化など、多彩な切り口から射水の楽しみ方を紹介しています。
items.description: 射水市ならではのユニークな魅力をテーマ別にまとめた特集ページです。海まちエリアや里まちエリア、おまつり、お土産・グルメ、歴史・文化など、多彩な切り口から射水の楽しみ方を紹介しています。
body_paragraphs: 射水市は、今も昔も文化の交差点。海・陸・川に結ばれ、日本各地、そして世界ともつながりながら、日々さまざまな交流が生まれてきました。時代ごとに新しいモノが集い、育まれ、発信され続けてきたからこそ、このまちにはユニークで愛おしい魅力がたっぷり詰まっています！
富山湾に面する射水の海辺には、雄大な自然と人々の暮らしが息づいています。帆船海王丸をシンボルとする海王丸パーク、漁師町の文化を受け継ぐ風情漂う内川周辺。射水らしさを体感するなら、まずこのエリアへ。水面に映る懐かしくも特別な風景が待っています。
新鮮な海の幸、里山で育まれる実り、そしてまちの人々が大切に作り、伝え続ける特産品の数々。射水には、土地の恵みを感じられる「おいしいもの」が揃っています。港町ならではのグルメを味わい、ユニークなおみやげを探す時間も旅の醍醐味。この土地ならではの味とぬくもりを、ぜひ現地で確かめてください。
射水の人々は、まつりのために日々を過ごしていると言っても過言ではありません。勇壮な獅子舞まつり、活気あふれる曳山まつり。ひとたび触れれば、世代を超えて受け継がれてきた伝統と熱気が、心に響くこと間違いなし！地元の人々と混ざり合いながら体感すれば、射水の「まつりの魂」を肌で感じることができるはず。
History, Culture, and Daily Life
射水市には、古くからの街道と、今も暮らしの中に息づくレトロな商店街があります。博物館や史跡を巡り、歴史を辿るというのも、ひと味違う特別な旅になるでしょう。また、里山の自然を生かした公園で体を動かすもよし、知る人ぞ知る絶景を訪れて撮影を楽しむもよし。あなただけの旅の物語を描いてみてください。
射水市を拠点に巡ることで、旅の魅力がぐっと広がる情報をご紹介します。射水旅にプラスするだけで、もっと楽くなること間違いなし！旅のおともにピッタリの観光パンフレットも、ぜひご覧ください。まずは射水から、富山を満喫してみませんか？

items.name_ja: おいしいものカレンダー
items.name: おいしいものカレンダー
items.description_ja: 射水市で味わえる海産物や農産物の旬を、月別カレンダーで紹介しています。富山湾のベニズワイガニやブリ、シロエビをはじめ、米や野菜、果物まで、季節ごとの「おいしい」を知ることができる食のガイドです。
items.description: 射水市で味わえる海産物や農産物の旬を、月別カレンダーで紹介しています。富山湾のベニズワイガニやブリ、シロエビをはじめ、米や野菜、果物まで、季節ごとの「おいしい」を知ることができる食のガイドです。
body_paragraphs: 射水市の新湊漁港が面する富山湾は、太平洋側の駿河湾、相模湾と並ぶ三大深湾のひとつで、水深1,200mを超える「天然のいけす」と称される豊かな漁場です。 その豊かさは、暖流の対馬海流と、低温の深層水である日本海固有水、さらに河川から運ばれる栄養分によって支えられており、暖流系・冷水系の多様な生物が共存する恵まれた海域となっています。 冬の寒ブリをはじめ、シロエビやベニズワイガニ、ホタルイカなど、四季折々の魚介類が水揚げされます。漁場が近いことから、早朝に加え季節によっては昼にも競りが行われ、早い時間から新鮮な魚が市内の食堂や寿司店に並びます。
※漁期以外の時期にも加工品や飲食店などで流通されるものもあります
新鮮な富山湾の幸に恵まれて生まれ育った射水市民が、普段どのように魚介を食べているのか？ある地元民のおすすめコメントとともに、射水市で食べられている主な魚介類をご紹介します。（コメントは一部の意見です。参考までにお楽しみのうえ、ぜひ現地でお召し上がりください）
「富山湾の宝石」と称されるシロエビ。安定して漁獲されるのは富山ならでは。まずは刺身で、コクのある上品な甘さを味わって！そしてバラエティ豊かなシロエビグルメを堪能してください。
射水といえば「ベニズワイガニ」と言っても過言ではないほど、どこよりも新鮮で美味しいベニズワイカニが食べられます。鮮度の良い素材ならではの味を楽しんだら、おみやげとしてもお求めください。
冬に富山湾で水揚げされるブリは、脂がたっぷりとのっており、格別の美味しさを誇ります。中でもブリトロは、濃厚な脂とやわらかな食感から特に人気の高い部位です。食べ方は刺身が主流ですが、近年ではブリしゃぶとしても楽しまれています。
富山湾のホタルイカは、3～5月の産卵期に漁獲されるため、他県産に比べて魚体が大きいのが特徴です。鮮度の良い状態で茹でたホタルイカは、外はプリプリとした食感、中はトロリとした濃厚な味わいで、獲れたてならではの美味しさは格別です。調理方法はボイルが主流ですが、沖漬けなどの加工品もあり、いずれも抜群の美味しさを楽しめます。

「白身魚の王様」と称されるのアカムツは、「白身のトロ」とも呼ばれるほど脂のりが良く、口の中でとろける極上の味わいが魅力の高級魚です。富山湾では一年を通して水揚げされますが、脂を蓄える7月～９月頃が最盛期とされています。主に定置網や刺網で漁獲されるため、身姿が美しいことから、刺身に適した良質なものが多く、塩焼きや煮付けでも楽しめます。スーパーにも並ぶことがある、身近に味わえる高級魚として親しまれています。
かつてゲンゲは、同じ水深に生息するホッコクアカエビを漁獲する際に混獲される“やっかいもの”とされ、「下の下の魚」として扱われていました。しかし近年では、コラーゲンをはじめとした豊富な栄養成分と美味しさが見直され、「幻魚」とも書かれるほど人気が高まっています。鮮度の良いものは刺身で味わうのが至高とされていますが、提供される機会は少なく、なかなか出会えない希少な味わいです。

富山県では名物「ますの寿司」に使われる魚として、サクラマスは古くから親しまれてきました。成熟すると体に桜色の婚姻色が現れ、桜の咲く頃に川へ遡上することから、その名が付けられています。しかし近年は環境の変化により個体数が減少し、環境省によって準絶滅危惧種にも指定されています。こうした背景から、射水市では養殖技術の研究が進められ、ブランド魚「いみずサクラマス」が誕生しました。上質な脂がほどよくのりながらも、もたれにくい上品な味わいが特徴で、新たな特産品として、刺身や寿司、焼き物など幅広い料理で楽しまれています。
新湊漁港では「マダイ」をはじめ「イシダイ（シマダイ）」、「アマダイ」、「クロダイ」、「メダイ」、「クルマダイ」など様々なタイが水揚げされます。そのどれもが新鮮で、刺身にすれば、身がしまり歯ごたえのあるイシダイや、もっちりとした弾力に、上品な甘みが広がるマダイなど、それぞれのタイが持つ個性豊かな味わいと食感が楽しめます。
地元ではフグ目カワハギ科の魚を総称して「カワハギ」と呼ぶことが多いですが、その中でも最もポピュラーなのが「ウマヅラハギ」です。面長の顔に小さな口、丸く愛嬌のある目が特徴で、どこかユーモラスな見た目をしています。しかし、その見た目とは裏腹に、分厚い皮を剥ぐと、さっぱりとしながらも甘みと旨みが詰まった上品な白身が現れます。寒さに耐えて引き締まった身に、濃厚な肝を和えた「肝和え」はまさに絶品です。
小さなツバイや、殻が大きくて薄く、しっかりとした歯ごたえのオオエッチュウバイなど様々なバイが水揚げされます。夏場の魚の漁獲が少ない時期に多く水揚げされることからも人気があり、煮付けや、近年ではツバイを用いた炊き込みご飯が人気です。刺身は漁場が近いため、臭みがなく特におすすめです。
富山湾の夏の味覚を代表するイワガキは、6～7月に盛漁期を迎えます。立山連峰をはじめとする山々から豊富な栄養分が注ぎ込む富山湾では、プランクトンが多く発生します。その栄養をたっぷり吸収して育つ天然のイワガキは、身が厚くジューシーで、濃厚な旨味と食べ応えのあるボリューム感が魅力です。生で食べるのが一般的ですが、フライや炭火焼でも美味しくいただけます。
鮮度の良いトヤマエビは特に絶品で、刺し身や寿司で食べることがおすすめ。タラバエビ科の中では大型で、食感もよく食べごたえもあります。焼くことで甘みが強まるため、塩焼きや炙りにも最適です。ミソの旨味も格別で、味噌汁などもエビの濃厚な旨味を感じられます。
ルビーのように鮮やかな赤い殻をむくと、薄ピンク色で透き通った身が現れ、とろけるような甘みが広がります。食べ方は刺身が一般的で、頭部は味噌汁の出汁として使うと、濃厚な旨味を楽しめます。新湊で水揚げされるものは身が大きく、食べごたえがあります。
射水市の庄川で育つ鮎は、清流の恵みで臭みが少なく、上品な香りとさわやかな味わいが特徴で香魚とも呼ばれます。身はほどよく締まり、餌となる藻類の影響で内臓まで美味しく、塩焼きにすると香ばしさと旨みが引き立ちます。小ぶりで骨までやわらかいため、頭から尾まで丸ごと食べられるのも魅力です。秋には卵を抱えた子持ち鮎となり、プチプチとした食感と濃厚な旨みを楽しめます。
シーズンごとに魚の旬は変わります。しかし、美味しい魚介をいつでも食べたい地元の人々は、それぞれの魚にあわせた加工方法、保存方法を発明してきました。 旬の季節の味わいはもちろんですが、季節が違うからといって食べないのはもったいない！カレンダーは参考までに、おいしい味を探しに来てくださいね。

肥沃な大地と庄川からの豊かな水に育まれた射水市の農産物は、県内でも高い評価を得ています。米どころとして知られ、コシヒカリを中心に味わい深いお米が収穫されるほか、四季折々の野菜や果物も豊富。特に小松菜や梨、枝豆などは地元直売所でも人気を集めています。農家が手間を惜しまず育てた安心・安全な農産品は、品質の高さから市外から訪れる人にも人気があり、地元の魅力を感じられる味わいとして多くの人に楽しまれています。
※出荷時期以外にも加工品や飲食店などで流通されるものもあります
地元農家が丹精込めて育てた、朝採れの新鮮な野菜や果物が店頭に並びます。
旬の野菜や加工品など、地元の恵みが勢ぞろい。毎月イベントも開催しています。
森の中にある小さなキノコハウス。新鮮なキノコを収穫して持ち帰りができるキノコ狩りも。季節に合った旬のキノコを収穫できます。
豊かな伏流水と肥沃な土壌で育つ自慢のお米。粒 立ちが良く、甘みと粘りのバランスに優れ、富山の食卓を支える味わいです。
濃厚なコクと香ばしさが特徴の黒大豆枝豆。深みのある味わいで、おやつやビールのお供に人気です。
射水市黒河地区のたけのこは、柔らかさとえぐみの少なさが自慢。春の訪れを感じる旬の味覚として親しまれています。
ビタミン豊富でクセがなく、幅広い料理に合う小松菜。通年収穫ができ、県内随一の生産量。地元の直売所でも人気の野菜で、日々の食卓に欠かせません。
小さな芽に栄養が凝縮されたスプラウト。健康志向の方に人気で、食卓に彩りを加える新鮮な食材です。
繊維がきめ細かく、シャキッとしながらも辛みが少なく、口当たりがやわらかいのが特徴です。
みずみずしさと上品な甘さの梨。食べごたえがあり、夏の贈答品としても人気を集めています。

items.name_ja: Travel ASAHI like a local
items.name: Travel ASAHI like a local
items.description_ja: 山と海に囲まれる、富山の東の入り口、朝日町の観光案内サイトです。ゆっくりとした時間が流れ、どこか懐かしい風景が漂うこの町で、ゆったりまったり、あさひの暮らしにふれる旅を。
items.description: 山と海に囲まれる、富山の東の入り口、朝日町の観光案内サイトです。ゆっくりとした時間が流れ、どこか懐かしい風景が漂うこの町で、ゆったりまったり、あさひの暮らしにふれる旅を。
body_paragraphs: あさひで暮らす人々とふれあいながら、この町の魅力をもっと感じられる時間を。
ヒスイ海岸を見渡せるヒスイテラスでは、さまざまなイベントに活用できるホール、サイクルステーションとしてレンタサイクル、調理場、シャワールーム等も完備。海遊び、ヒスイ探し、釣り、サイクリング、登山と朝日町での体験交流のビジターセンターとしてご活用いただけます。
地域のつながりを深めるお茶会は、山村で続く大切な生活文化です。蛭谷地区のおじいちゃんおばあちゃんが集う「バタバタ茶伝承館」で、バタバタ茶会の雰囲気を体験できます。
県下最古の江戸時代の町家「川上家」を歴史公園内に移築し、囲炉裏端で「バタバタ茶」を体験出来ます。初夏には、八重咲の蓮が咲き誇り、芝生広場の滑り台は子供たちに大人気です。
朝日町の国史跡不動堂遺跡や境A遺跡（共に縄文時代）、浜山玉つくり遺跡（古墳時代）の出土品を常設展示。本物を間近で見て、実際に勾玉作りや土器製作を体験できるプログラムもご用意しています。
「ふるさと美術館」が、旧なないろKANを改修して移転オープン。赤川焼の陶芸体験工房、朝日岳を眺望できる喫茶室など、周辺の歴史公園や不動堂遺跡などとあわせて、憩いの場として一体的にお楽しみください。
町出身の青柳政二が開館した古美術専門美術館。江戸時代の陶工・仁清の作品が充実。回遊式庭園を眺めながら、喫茶コーナーで安らぎのひと時を。鯉の餌やりも人気です。
旧金沢藩の十村役だった伊東家の旧家で、明治天皇巡幸のため、飛騨地方から檜の最高級材を取り寄せて明治11年に改修されました。天皇が宿泊された上座敷の壁一面には金箔が施してあり、随所に匠の技が光る由緒ある建物です。
ヒスイ海岸近くの国道8号沿いにあり交通アクセスも良く、日帰り温泉にも近いので、県内外から多くの方々にご利用いただいております。
「日本の渚百選」のヒスイ海岸が目の前に広がり、宿泊施設も充実しているキャンプ場。海水浴やBBQを楽しめ、釣りやウインドサーフィンなど、海辺の遊びが満喫出来ます。
ゴトウユニットの世界最高のスピーカーシステムが奏でる「音楽鑑賞会」、歌って健康を目指す「音夢くらぶ」、響きの良い小ホールならではの「サロンコンサート」を開催しています。
全国新酒鑑評会・金沢国税局新酒鑑評会連続金賞受賞！県下最古の酒蔵で最年少杜氏の「林酒造場」。境の関所で与力であった創業者が、酒を造りはじめたのが寛永3年。代表作の「黒部峡」は、手づくりに徹しているこだわりのお酒です。
農鍛冶職人 大久保中秋さん。終戦3日後の昭和20年8月18日に鍛冶屋へ弟子入り。以来、青函トンネル工事用の工具や、農作業用の鍬・鋤、職人用の出刃包丁、そして、全国にファンのいる「泊鉈」を作り続けています。
地産地消にこだわったふるさとの味、母の味をお届けします。漬物、味噌、切り餅、お菓子、惣菜、仕出し弁当など幅広く農林産物の加工に取り組んでいます。
農業をとおして小中学校への体験学習を受け入れ、地域へ貢献できる農園となりました。安心して食べる事のできるお米と野菜を作り、販売する会社としてがんばっています。
大浴場や温水プールの熱源に焼却熱を利用している大変エコな施設です。お子様からご年配の方まで、一日ゆっくり楽しめます。お食事のみのご利用も歓迎いたします。
朝日町立ふるさと美術館内の赤川焼陶芸体験工房では、ろくろや手びねりでの陶芸体験ができ、世代を超えて人気を博しています。
里山の笹川で笹川焼をする傍ら陶芸教室を開き、手づくりの楽しさを味わっていただいています。湯飲み、コーヒーカップ、花器、抹茶茶碗などの作品に挑戦できます。
越中宮崎駅前のお食事処 結では、名物タラ汁定食のほか軽食をご用意しています。ヒスイ海岸でとれたヒスイ原石等の展示販売や、お気に入りの石の加工が出来る工房「Jinen（ジネン）」もあります。
海の香り、山の息吹、湧き出る湯、100％天然温泉かけ流し、心ゆくまでおくつろぎください。

items.name_ja: 前沢牛
items.name: Maesawa Beef
items.description_ja: 上質できめ細やかな霜降りで、しっとりした肉質。脂はしつこくなく上質な香りが口の中に広がり、肉が溶けるように感じられる。全国肉用牛枝肉共励会においては、全国最多となる通算6回の名誉賞（農林水産大臣賞）を受賞するなど、数々の受賞歴を有する。
items.description: High-quality, finely marbled beef with a moist texture. The fat is not heavy, and a refined aroma spreads throughout the mouth, giving the impression that the meat melts. At the National Beef Carcass Competition, this beef has received the Honorary Prize (Minister of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries Award) a cumulative six times, the most of any producer nationwide, among numerous other awards.

items.name: Iwate Noda-mura Araumi Hotate
items.description_ja: プランクトンが豊富で自由に泳ぎ回れる環境下で養殖されたホタテガイ。身は肉厚で旨味が濃く、貝柱は繊維がしっかりとして弾力がある。貝殻は表面に付着した生物が丁寧に除去されているため美しい。
items.description: Scallops cultivated in an environment rich in plankton where they can swim freely. The flesh is thick with a rich umami flavor, and the adductor muscle has firm fibers and elasticity. The shells are beautiful because organisms attached to the surface have been carefully removed.

items.name_ja: 岩手木炭
items.name: Iwate Charcoal
items.description_ja: 炭質が硬く火持ちが良い。炭素割合は概ね90％（全国規格75％以上）と高く、燃焼時の煙や炎、臭いが最小限に抑えられ、燃焼後に残る灰も少ない。その品質は高く評価され、平成18年度から参加している農林水産祭において、農林水産大臣賞や林野庁長官賞を現在に至るまで毎年受賞。
items.description: The charcoal is hard in quality and burns for a long time. Its carbon content is approximately 90% (compared to the national standard of 75% or more), and smoke, flame, and odor during combustion are kept to a minimum, with little ash remaining after burning. Its quality is highly regarded, and since participating in the Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries Festival from fiscal year 2006, it has received the Minister of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries Award and the Director-General of the Forestry Agency Award every year up to the present.

items.description: Rich flavor with a smooth texture. Soft yet strongly sticky, and does not fall apart during cooking. Well-uniform in size and large-grained.

items.name: Joboji Urushi
items.description_ja: 硬化後の強度が非常に優れているうえに、安定した品質を有する漆。透明度、硬化時間、粘度等のバリエーションも豊富であることから、漆芸家や塗師、文化財修復職人などの需要者から高く評価。国宝や重要文化財など日本を代表する建造物の修理・修復に使用。
items.description: A lacquer with exceptionally high strength after hardening and stable quality. It is highly regarded by lacquer artists, lacquerers, and cultural property restoration craftspeople for its wide variety of options in terms of transparency, hardening time, viscosity, and other properties. Used in the repair and restoration of representative Japanese structures designated as National Treasures or Important Cultural Properties.

items.name_ja: 甲子柿
items.name: Kasshi Kaki
items.description_ja: 甲子柿は、岩手県釜石市甲子町を中心に、伝統製法で渋抜きされた、完熟トマトのような鮮紅色をし、ゼリーのような食感が特長の柿である。渋柿を室（むろ）の中に入れ、煙で燻す燻煙脱渋法で甘くした柿は甲子柿のみで、その珍しさが評価されている。古くから釜石地方独特の秋の味として親しまれてきた伝統産品である。
items.description: Kasshi Kaki is a persimmon produced mainly in Kasshi-cho, Kamaishi City, Iwate Prefecture, using traditional methods to remove astringency. It is characterized by a vivid crimson color resembling a fully ripe tomato and a jelly-like texture. It is the only persimmon sweetened by the smoke-fumigation astringency-removal method, in which astringent persimmons are placed in a sealed room (muro) and smoked; this rarity is highly regarded. It is a traditional product that has long been cherished as a distinctive autumn flavor of the Kamaishi region.
items.production_area_text: 岩手県釜石市

items.name: Hirota Bay Ishikage Clam
items.description_ja: 殻表は濃い赤茶色で、形はふっくらとしており、クリーム色の足の部分を食す。遊離アミノ酸の割合が高く、弾力があり、甘みと旨味が特徴。鮮度が良く、特有の甘みがあり、希少価値が高く、都内の高級料亭や寿司店で欠かせない商品となっている。
items.description: The shell surface is a deep reddish-brown, and the shape is plump. The cream-colored foot portion is the edible part. Characterized by a high proportion of free amino acids, a firm and elastic texture, sweetness, and umami. The clam is fresh, has a distinctive sweetness, and is of high rarity value, making it an indispensable item at high-end traditional restaurants and sushi establishments in Tokyo.

items.name: Nishi Warabi
items.description_ja: 太くて長いわらびで、水煮にすると「とろっ」とした食感で柔らかく、うま味成分が豊富でアクやスジが極めて少ない。他産地のわらびに比べ高値で取引されるなど、需要者から高く評価されるとともに、地域の食文化とのつながりも深い。「西わらび」の根茎についても、地域の特産品である「わらび餅」などの原料として活用されている。
items.description: A thick and long bracken fern that, when boiled in water, has a smooth and soft texture, is rich in umami components, and has very little bitterness or fibrous strands. It is highly valued by buyers and traded at higher prices than bracken from other producing regions. It also has deep ties to the local food culture. The rhizomes of Nishi Warabi are also utilized as an ingredient in local specialty products such as 'warabi mochi' (bracken starch cake).

items.name: Kawai Red Perilla
items.description_ja: 葉の表が緑色で裏が赤紫色という全国的にも類を見ない「片面紫蘇(かためんしそ)」。葉に厚みがあるため、一般的な「しそ」に比べ、葉一枚あたりの重量が1.2～1.8倍で、香りが強い。塩蔵品は、漬物等の強い発色を促し、香りも強いため、「紀州南高梅」の原料として用いられている。また、地域で商品化した「しそジュース」は人気の特産品として定着している。
items.description: A uniquely distinctive variety known as 'single-sided perilla' (katamen shiso), found nowhere else in Japan, in which the front of the leaf is green and the back is red-purple. Because the leaves are thick, each leaf weighs 1.2 to 1.8 times more than that of ordinary perilla, and the aroma is strong. Salt-preserved products promote vivid coloring in pickles and similar foods and have a strong aroma, making them an ingredient used in 'Kishu Nanko plums.' In addition, 'perilla juice' commercialized in the region has become established as a popular local specialty.

items.description_ja: 岩手県は八幡平のスキー、奥入瀬渓流でのトレッキング、三陸海岸でのサーフィンや海水浴、そして豊かな自然の中でのキャンプなど多彩なアウトドアアクティビティが楽しめます。
items.description: 岩手県は八幡平のスキー、奥入瀬渓流でのトレッキング、三陸海岸でのサーフィンや海水浴、そして豊かな自然の中でのキャンプなど多彩なアウトドアアクティビティが楽しめます。
body_paragraphs: 当サイトを使用することにより、クッキーの設定および使用に同意したことになります。 詳細については、プライバシーポリシーを参照してください。
柳田國男の著書「遠野物語」の舞台である遠野市に佇む、築70年の一棟貸切の宿「リアン遠野」。日本の原風景と呼ばれる古くから変わらぬ美しい田園風景と、懐かしさを感じる古民家は、滞在する人を「遠野物語」の世界に誘います。”物語を感じる”ここでしかできないリアルな体験をしてみませんか？
清冽な流れが長い年月をかけて見事なまでに渓谷美を造りだした厳美渓。古都平泉や厳美渓を心ゆくまで堪能したら、のんびりお湯につかりたい。
毎分720リットルの湧出量を誇り、源水100％で循環（ろ過）も加温も消毒もせず、一滴の水も加えない源泉を「かけ流し」にした温泉です。リハビリ効果のある歩き湯もあります。栗駒ゴルフ倶楽部隣接。
栗駒山の北麓、標高1,125ｍに位置する須川温泉は湧出量毎分6,000リットルの温泉。その歴史は古く、徳川時代から300年間以上もの間、みちのくの名湯として親しまれている。泉質は日本でも稀な強酸性のミョウバン緑ばん泉で、古くから湯治客が多く、特にリウマチ性疾患、慢性中毒症などに効果がある。雄大な自然の中に千人風呂、家族風呂、名物のおいらん風呂（蒸し風呂）もおすすめ。
あづまね温泉はアルカリ性単純温泉で、入浴すると肌がツルツルすることから美人の湯として親しまれています。３時間は湯冷めしないと定評です。 ききょう荘は、自炊も出来る静かな保養施設です。宿泊も出来ます。
一戸インターまたは浄法寺インターから峠を越えて辿り着く宮田温泉。付近には岩魚が釣れる清流が流れ木々に囲まれ恵まれた環境に佇む。泉質は『美人の湯』と言われる重曹（炭酸水素ナトリウム）を多量に含みお湯はツルツルとした肌触り。また食塩分も比較的多くリウマチなどに効能がある。二酸化炭素の含有量も多いので血行を良くし体がよく温まるという。近くの町から定期的に通ってくる常連客もいるほど。
和洞年間（708～715年）に発見され古くは亭沢温泉とよばれていた。江戸時代に入り「山ノ神信仰」により一般の入浴が禁止され周辺に網を張ったのが「網張」の由来とされる。泉質は単純酸性・硫黄温泉低張性酸性高温泉、効能は慢性皮膚病・慢性婦人病・きりきず・糖尿病・高血圧症・痔病など。
標高1,400m、東日本で最も高いところにある温泉。春は春スキー、秋には蓬莱境を訪れる人々の基地となっている。
県立花巻広域公園内にある温泉で、公共の宿。肌触りの良い温泉と県産食材を使用した四季折々の和食膳を堪能できます。 公園内ということもあり運動広場のほかテニスコート、ゴルフ場が完備されています。

The area extends around Morioka, the prefectural capital.To the west is Towada-Hachimantai National Park, and breathtaking views surround the area around Mt. Iwate, also known as the Nanbu Fuji, and Hachimantai. Along the central flow of the Kitakami River and the surrounding rural landscapes, various onsen await across the abundant land, showcasing the ever-changing expressions of the four seasons amidst the rich and bountiful nature.Enjoy sake, wine, beer, and other locally brewed alcoholic beverages, as well as traditional cuisine.
Customers who have tasted our Wanko Soba say, ``It's a delicious specialty.''

"Roadside Station Nishinine" is located along National Route 282. Along with specialty products and a souvenir corner, the city's agricultural and livestock products are sold. The most appealing part is the fresh vegetables. They also sell specialty spinach, cabbage, green peppers, and wild vegetables. In addition, the ingredients in the cafeteria mainly use vegetables, meat, eggs, etc. produced in Hachimantai City. Spinach curry and spinach soft serve ice cream are popular.
Approximately 30 minutes by car from the center of Morioka city. This slope is perfect for beginners to practice and for children. Fully equipped with night game equipment.
ANA Holiday Inn Resort Appi Kogen “Hills Building”

On December 16, 2021, the name was changed from "Appi Hills Shirakaba no Mori" and "Appi Kogen Onsen Hotel." This is a resort hotel consisting of two buildings: the ``Hot Spring Building,'' which is connected by a passageway to ``Shirakaba no Yu,'' which has one of the largest open-air baths in Tohoku, and the ``Hills Building,'' which is directly connected to the ski resort.

To commemorate the souls of the Takuboku couple, a statue of Takuboku Bokyo was erected on the top of the rocky mountain, Takuboku Bokyo Hill, overlooking the local mountains and rivers. The statue faces his hometown, Mt. Himekami, and is engraved with one of Takuboku's favorite poems, ``In autumn, I listen to the insects that fill the three fields at the foot of Mt. Iwate.'' Nearby, a ``couple poem monument'' of a poet and his wife was erected, one of a kind in Japan, and Takuboku's ``When I see the mountains of my hometown far to the north through the train window, I straighten my neck,'' and his wife Setsuko's ``Hikari.'' Two poems are engraved on it: ``From the faint sound of crickets in the evening, the arrival of autumn, and the embrace of my heart.'' The two of them, both young and only in their 20s, fell ill due to poverty and passed away one after another, and now they are gazing at the mountains and rivers of their hometown in the form of songs.
Iwate Prefectural Civic Center

The Iwate Prefectural Civic Center plays a central role in Iwate Prefecture's artistic culture, and is used for multiple purposes such as music, theater, and gatherings. The bronze statue ``Habataki'' created by Yasutake Funakoshi, which stands on the front right, symbolizes the rapid growth of Iwate's artistic culture.

The area has a well-balanced blend of industry and agriculture, and is dotted with numerous historic sites.Remains and relics, including the World Heritage Site of Hiraizumi, tell us of the existence of a once flourishing culture. The region is also known nationwide for its abundance of diverse cultural intangible assets, including but not limited to Hanamaki City, associated with Kenji Miyazawa who referred to Iwate as Ihatove, and Tono, a folktale village made famous from Tono monogatari (The Legends of Tono), as well as other cultural treasures involving folktales and traditional festivals. Many onsen towns such as Hanamaki, Ichinoseki, and Nishiwaga can be found in the area. A journey exploring these uniquely charming onsen is highly recommended.
Used with permission of Chūson-ji Temple
Ichinoseki/Senmaya Sake no Kura Exchange Facility

This is a historical, cultural, and tourist exchange facility that utilizes the former Yokoya Sato family residence, a nationally registered tangible cultural property. Inside the facility, you can tour and walk around the Taisho era-filled atmosphere, which is centered around a stately main building built with an earthenware storehouse made with plenty of zelkova wood, and a Western building built in modern Western architecture, as well as a cluster of sake breweries that still produce traditional sake. In addition, live concerts are held at the Tozo Live Hall (accommodates over 200 people) and the Shinkura Live Hall (accommodates 40 people), both of which utilize sake breweries.
Famous confectionery Benkei Chikaramochi

This is the signature sweet from Yoshinoya, a long-established confectionery shop in Hiraizumi town that has been in business since 1919. Benkei Chikaramochi is a walnut-yubeshi sweet that has been loved since its founding, without changing its recipe or taste.

A free rest facility located in front of the gate of Shoboji Temple in the back. In addition to souvenir items, there is also a soba restaurant and cafe. From Mizusawa-Esashi Station, transfer to the Iwate Prefectural Transportation Haneda Ofunato Line Mizusawa Ekidori bus stop and head to the Shohoji bus stop.

Approximately 200 types of alpine plants grow on Mt. Hayachine, which is one of the richest in Japan in terms of variety and quantity, and is also famous for its many unique varieties. Among them, the Hayachineus snowsou is famous as the representative flower of Hayachine, and it closely resembles the edelweiss that blooms in the Alps. The colorful and pretty flowers never cease to fascinate climbers.
Bathhouse (self-catering) [Osawa Onsen]
The self-catering club is located in a building that is over 200 years old and is associated with Kenji Miyazawa. You can make your own meals or have three meals at a restaurant.
Oshu Senbei specialty store Senya

Received the highest gold award at the World Monde Selection for 5 consecutive years. The main ingredient is Hitomebore, which is cultivated in the clear air and water of Oshu, and each piece is baked with great care by our craftsmen for an authentic taste.
Suna Yukko [Tsukizawa Onsen] (Day trip bathing facility)

"Sunayukko" is a wooden building with a tongari roof and wooden walls that blend in with the mountain surroundings. This is the first sand bath in Tohoku. Heat natural silica sand produced in the town with hot spring water, and bury yourself completely in it to warm your body. There is also a large bath and a rest room.

Tono City has developed as a castle town of 12,000 koku, and has become a hub of trade connecting the inland and coastal regions, attracting many goods and people, and has become a bustling city with a variety of merchant houses. The Castle Town Museum introduces Tono during the Edo period by displaying maps of castle processions and many preserved historical items.

The area includes Kuji City, known for being the filming site for the TV drama Amachan, the World Heritage Site of Goshono Ruins, and Ninohe City, the northern gateway to Iwate.Buddhist temples like Tendaiji Temple and the intricate lacquerware of Joboji nuri tell us tales of history and culture. Meanwhile, grains from the inland regions and seafood from the coastal areas are certain to delight the palate. The inland area is surrounded by nature, and Mt. Orizume, covered with beech forests, is one of the largest habitats for fireflies in Japan.

Suki konbu is made by drying kelp that has been cut into 2-3 mm pieces and made into sheets. Sukikonbu is synonymous with Fudai Village, so much so that some people won't buy it unless it's produced in Fudai. The nutritious and high-quality kelp grown in the Fudai Sea is carefully processed without sparing any effort. It is known for its beautiful green color and soft texture, and for its high quality. We are proud of our kelp, which ranks among the top in production and sales in the prefecture. It is sure to be useful in a variety of situations, such as stir-fried, seafood salad, side dishes, and boiled tofu.

A gallery run by Yukiya Izumida, a ceramic artist from Rikuzentakata City who has received high praise in numerous contests. In addition to soil from Noda Village, he continues to create works with a focus on local materials, such as using loose ore from the Noda Tamagawa Mine. Here you can purchase a variety of carefully crafted and fired works, ranging from highly artistic items to practical items. The Nodayaki workshop is adjacent to the Asian Folk Art Museum. You can also make a reservation and try your hand at making one-of-a-kind Nodayaki.

This is the spot where the Sanriku Railway crosses the railway bridge with the Pacific Ocean in the background. This 30-meter-high railroad bridge is located south of Sanriku Railway's Horiuchi Station. It is said to be one of the most famous spots along the Sanriku Railway line. The train stops for about one minute on the bridge to provide tourists with an ocean view. In the drama "Amachan," the scene of Natsubappa waving the big fishing flag was filmed on the beach below. It is also a popular spot for photo enthusiasts looking for shutterbug opportunities from near National Route 45. Basic Information
A long-established Nanbu rice cracker shop in Ninohe City that has been in business for 51 years. We make traditional Nanbu rice crackers one by one by hand.

A restaurant where you can feel the warmth of wood in the image of a mountain hut. We offer Mamebu, a local dish from Yamagata Town (formerly Yamagata Village) in Kuji City, as well as Genghis Khan set meals and ramen.
Nanbu Senbei, known as Iwate Prefecture's famous confectionery, is made all over the prefecture and continues to maintain its traditional taste.

It was named ``Fukurai,'' a sake that brings happiness, so that it brings good fortune to everyone, including those who drink it, those who sell it, and those who make it. ``Fukurai'' is brewed with high-quality groundwater from a clean area and the traditional techniques of Nanbu chief brewers. It is also appreciated as a gift as a lucky charm. [Main products] Fukugita

Miyata Onsen can be reached by crossing a mountain pass from Ichinohe Interchange or Joboji Interchange. It stands in a blessed environment surrounded by trees and a clear stream where you can catch rockfish. The quality of the spring water is said to be ``beauty hot water'' as it contains a large amount of baking soda (sodium bicarbonate) and has a smooth texture. It is also relatively high in salt, which is effective against rheumatism. It also has a high carbon dioxide content, which improves blood circulation and warms the body. There are even regular customers who come from nearby towns on a regular basis.
A rustic flavor made by stuffing millet and barley bean sprouts over a period of about two weeks. It also goes great with Nanbu rice crackers.

In 2021, a tourist farm has opened in Rikuzentakata City where you can enjoy a strawberry picking experience. This tourist farm is operated by Seseragi, a type B business that supports continued employment. The facility is equipped to allow people in wheelchairs to pick strawberries, so anyone can enjoy strawberry picking. Please try and compare the 10 different varieties.

The fragrant ``june mochi'' is grilled one by one over charcoal. ``June'' refers to perilla, which is made by rubbing the self-grown perilla, adding sugar and sake, and applying it generously to the mochi. This is a popular item and is only sold on Saturdays and Sundays. Other freshly harvested vegetables are also sold at reasonable prices.

Yakiniku cold noodle restaurant. A facility where you can experience manufacturing Miyako's processed seafood products and eating fishermen's food. The museum also displays and sells seasonal live fish, seaweed, and processed products.

Directly managed by a dairy farmer in the town, this ice cream has a rich flavor and is made with a combination of pasteurized milk, which takes care of the milk's original nutrition and flavor, and Shizukuishi's vegetables and fruit trees.

A tourist farm where you can experience picking blueberries while looking out at Mt. Iwate. We offer over 1000 large blueberries. There is also a cafeteria where you can enjoy a dessert menu using blueberries, and it is a wonderful space where you can relax and enjoy nature. Azumane Onsen is an alkaline simple hot spring that is well known as a beauty's hot spring because it makes the skin smooth and smooth after bathing. Kikyoso is a quiet recreation facility where you can cook your own meals. Lodging is also available.

The first inn in Ichinoseki Onsenkyo from the city. Kamenoi Hotel (formerly Kanpo no Yado Ichinoseki) is located on a hill along National Route 342 that leads to Kurikoma Quasi-National Park, on the land of Horyu, where a dragon once ascended to heaven and brought rain.The view is spectacular. Relaxing in the Takara-no-Yu, enjoying the lingering snow and fresh greenery of Mt. Kurikoma in May, and the fall foliage in autumn, will surely stir up the romance of your trip. The spacious hot springs are also pleasant, and you can enjoy relaxing and relaxing after walking around the Oshu Fujiwara clan ruins and Genbikei Valley. Best time to see autumn leaves: Mid-October to early November
At an altitude of 1,400m, this hot spring is the highest in eastern Japan. It is a base for people who visit spring skiing in the spring and Horaikyo in the fall.
Kanaya Onsen Hotel Ginga Park Hanamaki

A public inn and hot spring located within Hanamaki Prefectural Park. You can enjoy the soothing hot springs and seasonal Japanese cuisine made with local ingredients. Since it is located within a park, there is a sports field, tennis courts, and a golf course.
Sannozan Onsen Zuisenkyo (formerly Yabitsu Onsen Zuisenkaku)

The facility name has changed from May 1, 2017. (Formerly Yabitsu Onsen Zuisenkaku) A hot spring inn located approximately 2km downstream from Yabitsu Dam. It provides a magnificent view of Mt. Sanno, where Jikaku Daishi is said to have lived in the past. The spring quality is a sodium/calcium chloride sulfate hot spring, and we are proud of the hot water. The large bath, "Zuisen no Yu," and other open-air baths lined with rocks blend seamlessly into the surrounding nature of Mt. Zuisan, giving you a taste of the four seasons. The Japanese-style guest rooms are filled with the scent of fresh wood. The season of fresh green leaves and autumn leaves is especially beautiful. Best time to see autumn leaves: Mid-October to early November

Esashi beef is raised with care, one by one, and fed with high-quality rice straw and hay produced in the fertile land of the Kitakami River basin. With just the right amount of marbling, it is truly a piece of meat art.

Cold noodles originally originated in the northern part of the Korean peninsula, but Teruto Aoki, who was originally from Hamheung in the northern part of the peninsula and immigrated to Japan, opened a restaurant called "Shodoen" in Morioka in 1955 (which still exists today). Cold noodles have appeared in Morioka, including (now open). At that time, cold noodles from Pyongyang had been introduced to Japan, but Mr. Aoki mixed the flavor of the spicy cold noodles from his hometown, Hamheung, with the light, non-spicy cold noodles from Pyongyang, and this is how Morioka cold noodles began. Since the 1960s, cold noodle shops have opened one after another in the Morioka area, each creating new flavors, and from the 1980s onwards, with the gourmet boom, ``Morioka cold noodles'' suddenly became known throughout the country. Morioka cold noodles are made with wheat flour and potato starch, so the noodles are characterized by their strong chewiness. The soup is made by boiling beef or chicken, seasoning it, and chilling it, and it blends with the spiciness of kimchi. There are approximately 30 cold noodle shops in the city.

The cafeteria, which has about 100 seats, offers ``healthy Tsubakiju cuisine'' made with seafood from the sea and mountains of Mt.Ofunato, as well as menus featuring plenty of abalone and scallops. In addition, at the confectionery workshop, you can try your hand at painting ``ikaka crackers'' with chocolate pens, and eat them freshly baked. The Yarimizu is a waterway used to draw mountain water into the pond. The bottom of the water is paved with cobblestones, and the meandering stream is lined with stonework such as mizukiri, mizukoshi, and mizukawari, which together with the seasonal flowers and plants along the water's edge make a wonderful sight. The "Kyokusui no En" is an elegant recreation of a Heian-period banquet, in which visitors recite waka poems as they float their sake cups on a stream. It is held on the fourth Sunday of May every year.

Six years have passed since the closure of the former Morioka Bus Center, which was popular for its retro flavor and “emoness.” On October 4, 2020, the long-awaited Shin Morioka Bus Center reopened after renovations. The two buildings, divided into east and west, are equipped with a bus terminal, bus waiting room, market, food hall, childcare support center, and hotel. A local hub that connects people with the charm of the region has begun to move strongly.

The entire bus terminal is completely covered by a roof, making boarding and alighting convenient on days when the weather is bad. In the waiting room, the benches used in the old bus center have been beautifully reupholstered and are still in use.

The Marche is located on the 1st floor of the east building and is a place where you can feel free to stop by and use it not only when using the bus, but also when you are not using the bus. “Fukuda Pan” is a popular shop that sandwiches the ingredients on the spot. Since we are open from early morning, many people are buying it for breakfast on this day too!
From lunch to drinks at night, this food hall on the second floor of the east building will make you want to crawl around the floor.
The iron logo of the old bus center is displayed on the wall on the second floor! Even the scratches and peeling paint are medals that tell the story of more than half a century of history.
Even after the renewal, the logo design has remained unchanged. It’s very modern and nice.

HOTEL MAZARIUM on the 3rd floor has a spa with an authentic Finnish sauna. Towels and bath towels are free, so you can use them empty-handed! If you use a long-distance bus, it’s a good idea to self-serve in the early morning or late at night, or usually on your way home from work.

The walls of the large lounge are filled with wall art created in a workshop to commemorate the opening. At the attached Toshiko Akiyoshi Jazz Museum, valuable record jackets and stage costumes are on display.
A sunset view with warm light that makes you feel relieved. The reborn Morioka Bus Center seems to have lit a light of memory and hope.
From here, a new Morioka story begins again!
The hexagonal gazebo full of Taisho romance has been a beloved symbol of the area for over 100 years.

After its role as a fire station, it was reopened in March 2020 as an exchange and experience facility. You will be greeted by a tasteful space with original granite cobblestone pavement and uniquely warped window glass. Morioka City Landscape Important Building.

Relax with the cafe’s original blended coffee and cake. Handmade paper cutting is retro and cute! In addition to exhibiting and selling craft works, we also hold hands-on classes such as hata weaving. (Holidays only/advance reservation required)

When it comes to Iwate souvenirs, the classic one is Nanbu rice crackers. Established in 1933, our diverse lineup includes traditional “Gomasabei” as well as peanut, pumpkin, walnut, cheese and coffee flavors, all handmade using local Nanbu ground flour.
If you are not sure which one to choose, consult the poster girl! While talking with Akane, the granddaughter of the founder, Ae Shirasawa, Sobachi was very satisfied with the selection.
Long-established Shirasawa Senbei shop

A street lined with elegant lattice doors, with the Nakatsugawa River in the background. Morikyu Shoten, which makes you want to just pop in, is nicknamed “Gozakyu.” Folk crafts, traditional bamboo baskets, easy-to-use brooms, straw slippers, etc. It is full of items that are easy to fit into modern life and that you will love.
The historic storefront is an important building in Morioka City’s landscape that still retains the image of a wealthy merchant in the late Edo period.

It was designed by Kingo Tatsuno, who designed the Bank of Japan head office and Tokyo Station, and Manji Kasai, a Morioka native, and was completed in 1909. After being used as a bank for over 100 years until 2012, it underwent restoration and opened as a public facility in 2016. The gorgeous corridor surrounding the atrium and the stately interior create an elegant space that will make your heart soar just by placing yourself there. Sobachi looks small here!
The red brick, white granite, and green dome are very impressive. As a typical landscape of Morioka, it is often depicted on postcards. Nationally designated important cultural property.

One of the oldest establishments in Morioka, where the coffee shop culture of the good old days remains. Established in 1950, the classical store, which is a renovated storehouse, allows time to flow slowly.

On this day, I had Hayashi beef rice and my favorite cream soda. The pizza toast is also melty and fluffy. The original parfait and cream anmitsu are also popular, making this a pure cafe that continues to be loved by generations.

Hotline Kamecho is the only shopping street in Iwate Prefecture that is an all-weather pedestrian arcade (10:00-21:00). It originates from the fact that in the past, many merchants dealing in fresh fish and dried goods lived there, and today there are about 80 stores of various categories in an area with a total length of 365 meters. With the renovation of Morioka Bus Center, it looks like it will become a hot spot again!

When Takuboku Ishikawa and Kenji Miyazawa spent their impressionable youth, Morioka was being reborn as a modern city with modern Western-style architecture. The former 90th Bank, which was completed in 1903, is also a representative example. Measures were taken to preserve and utilize it, and it took on its current appearance in 2002. The first floor has permanent exhibitions, and the second floor holds art exhibitions, concerts, and other events. Nationally designated important cultural property.
The light and sound experience room “Subaru” is a space that used to be a vault. Take a 5-minute time trip on the imaginary Galaxy Express.
The tea set at “Kissa Akogare” comes with simple Morioka sweets.

On November 24, 2020, the Azumaya main store completed its first renovation in 85 years. “Nanbu Soba Furi” is a simple Kaiseki meal. You can enjoy soba in a variety of ways, including bamboo steamer, kake, buckwheat, and crepe.

The most popular item for lunch is the “Special Katsudon”, which has an exquisite taste that is made with the dashi soup that is unique to soba restaurants and the accent of pepper. The new store has a counter and private rooms, and is likely to attract more and more customers.

Morioka City is currently attracting attention as it was featured in the New York Times article “52 Places to Visit in 2023”*. This time, we will introduce Morioka’s many highlights, along with the nearby recommended spot, Nagayama Kaido in Shizukuishi Town.
*Reference article https://www.city.morioka.iwate.jp/kankou/kankou/kankouinfo/1041747/index.html Please also take a look at the “Morioka Town Walk 2023 Special Feature”!

A small art museum located on the banks of the Nakatsugawa River that flows through the city of Morioka. The works of Beniko Fukazawa, a painter from Morioka who continued to paint wildflowers, and her husband Shozo are on display, changing with the seasons. From the cafe on the first floor, you can spend a relaxing time while looking out at the Nakatsu River flowing in front of you. (The cafe menu is currently unavailable.) We also have picture postcards and notepads, so please take them as souvenirs.

Kogensha published Kenji Miyazawa’s only collection of children’s stories during his lifetime, “Restaurant with Many Orders.” Currently, it is a store that sells handmade items from all over the country. A variety of buildings are connected by a courtyard, including “Kohikan”, a coffee room with a pleasant atmosphere decorated with stained glass, “Campanella”, where foreign folk art is displayed, and “Majielkan”, a museum dedicated to Kenji Miyazawa. It looks like a small town. There is also a product store called “Morio” across from the main building.

Morioka dagashi began as a preserved food in cold climates. Sekiguchi-ya Confectionery was founded in 1899, and is now in its fourth generation, which continues to cherish the taste of handmade products using all natural ingredients without using additives. Simple flavors such as miso bread, tankiri, and ishigoromo are popular, and shochuto is a colorful and cute-looking sweet. It is a sweet made by boiling down sugar and adding shochu inside.It is very delicate and difficult to handle, so it is a valuable sweet that can only be found in a limited number of places in Morioka City.

Morioka City Central Park is located south of Morioka Station and is home to cultural facilities such as the Iwate Prefectural Museum of Art. BeBA TERRACE (Morioka City Central Park Viva Terrace) is an area developed with the aim of providing a place for people of all generations to enjoy, connect, and learn from each other. Within the area, there is a “Manabi Building” that houses a Western confectionery shop and a homespun workshop, a “Food and Beverage Building” that houses a udon shop and a cafe, a gallery of Nanbu ironware, and fresh produce grown by farmers near Morioka City. There are many direct sales stands selling fruits and vegetables.

A hot spring that is popular as the inner parlor of Morioka. It is said that the name “Tsunagi” came from the fact that a long time ago, Minamoto no Yoshiie would tie his beloved horse here to rest. There are inns and hotels overlooking Lake Gosho, which was created by damming the Shizukuishi River, and nearby are Morioka Handmade Village, Koiwai Farm, and areas around Lake Gosho where families can enjoy nature.

One of the largest gardening specialty stores in Tohoku. On the vast grounds of 3,000 square meters, we sell seeds, seedlings, and gardening goods, and there is an English garden full of nature. In particular, Shibazakura no Oka in mid-May is spectacular, with the entire area dyed pink against the still-snow-covered Mt. Iwate in the background. The adjacent “Farmhouse Restaurant Rara” serves local cuisine using locally sourced ingredients as much as possible. For the rice, we use our home-grown rice, “Ginga no Shizuku.”

5 minutes by car from Koiwai Farm. This shop sells home-roasted coffee beans, located in a quiet forest surrounded by trees. High-quality raw beans are carefully roasted using a roasting machine located in a quiet corner of the store, and the aroma of coffee wafts through the air. From the window seats, you can enjoy beautiful views of the four seasons, and enjoy delicious coffee and sweets while relaxing.

A small cafe run by a wild grape farmer, 5 minutes by car from Koiwai Farm. All menu items using home-grown wild grapes are popular. “Nonoka Parfait” is a rich cheesecake with lots of homemade wild grape ice cream and berries that bring out the natural sourness and sweetness of wild grapes! This is a comfortable cafe where you can enjoy the magnificent view of Yama Vineyard and Mt. Iwate from the counter seats.
Yamabudo Farm Cafe Nonoka (Yamabudo Farm Cafe Nonoka)

A log house standing in the middle of nature. The inside of the store is a space where you can feel the warmth of wood. Authentic pizza baked in a stone oven at high temperatures is crispy on the outside and chewy on the inside! Seasonal pizzas made with wild vegetables such as Bakke (Japanese butterbur) are popular, but we also recommend standard menu items such as stone-oven curry doria and hand-kneaded hamburgers. Why not stop by on your drive?

Exquisite! Iwate’s liquor special – beer

Morioka City was featured in the New York Times article ``52 Places to Visit in 2023''*, and a temporary tourist information center has been set up inside Morioka Station, creating a welcoming atmosphere. This time, we would like to introduce the northern part of the Sanriku coast facing the Pacific Ocean, which is about 1.5 to 2 hours by car from Morioka. In addition to Sanriku's beautiful natural scenery, we have also covered gourmet spots that have not been introduced much before. It's also a good idea to plan your schedule around festivals and events. Please use this information to plan your trip from Morioka to Sanriku.
*Reference article (city.morioka.iwate.jp)
Travel time from Morioka Station

■Miyako Station: Approximately 1 hour and 40 minutes by express bus 106 / Approximately 2 hours and 20 minutes by JR Yamada Line / Approximately 1 hour and 20 minutes by car ■Ryusendo Cave: Approximately 2 hours by bus/approximately 1 hour and 50 minutes by car ■Kuji Station: Approximately 2 hours 45 minutes by bus (via Shirakaba/Kuzumaki) / Approximately 2 hours 25 minutes by bus (via Kuji Kohaku/Kunohe)/ Approximately 2 hours 30 minutes by car

*Sanriku Coastal Road has “half interchange (IC)” and “full interchange”. A half IC is an interchange where you can enter and exit in only one direction, either the up or down line. Please be careful when using.
For more information, please check the Sanriku Coastal Road MAP (Sanriku National Highway Office homepage) .
*The contents posted are from June 5th and June 6th, 2023.

About 300 years ago, the seventh priest of Miyakoyama Joanji Temple, Reikyo, exclaimed, “It’s just like the Pure Land,” and Jodogahama Beach is a nationally designated scenic spot that got its name. The spectacular view that spreads out in front of you is truly breathtaking. It has a scale that cannot be conveyed in photos, and is a place you should definitely visit at least once.

The white rhyolite and green pine trees are reflected on the rippling surface of the water, and you will be mesmerized by the various nuances of the color of the sea. In the summer, the beach is crowded with many swimmers.

“Miyako Umineko Maru” started operating in July 2022 as Miyako City’s new sightseeing boat. The refreshing coloring of white and the regional color “Jodogahama Eternal Green” defined by the Japan Regional Color Association is very charming!

You can board from two departure points: Dezaki Wharf and Jodogahama (pier), and the excursion course (about 30 minutes) takes you to Omote Jodogahama, Koyasu Jizo, Ura Jodogahama, Candle Rock, a nationally designated natural monument, etc. , you can also listen to the guide about Sanriku Geopark and geosites, which is very satisfying. When you step out onto the spacious observation deck, the background music is “Miyako Pleasure Boat Ondo.” A must-have fun is playing with the flying gulls while holding “Umineko Bread” (¥200).

I was surprised by the reasonably priced Chirashi (¥1,600), which was packed with toppings…Isn’t it the best value for money? There is a wide selection of nigiri sushi, rice bowls, noodle menus, and set meals, so if you are unsure, come here! It’s understandable that there are many people who say so.
Is there a mysterious bread in Miyako City that sells out as soon as it opens in the morning? ! That is this “dressing” (¥320).

As the name suggests, Les de Chevre (Goat’s Milk), this patisserie is famous for its Western sweets made with goat milk produced at the company’s Happiness Farm. The eye-catching character, Yvonne the goat, has many fans, and there are many stylish goods available.

In search of “Goat Milk Cream Bread”, which is ordered from all over the country, I walked 2 minutes to “POST BAKERY”, an affiliated store. The rich yet light aftertaste makes it perfect for both meals and snacks. The “Baby Yagi Bread Set” (¥1,350), which comes in a pack of 5 pieces (¥1,950) and a variety of mini-sized breads, is sure to get compliments as a souvenir.

Ride on the Les de Chevres wrapped train and enjoy a 2-hour all-you-can-eat sweets buffet made with goat milk + a souvenir included. You can even meet the goat stationmaster who comes to work from the farm! *The last service will be on Saturday, August 12th.

A new social hub in Ryusendo Cave, with a blue logo that looks like spreading ripples and a hope that many people will gather and share smiles. The shop area will be pre-opening in April 2023, and even Sobachi, who visited for the first time, can’t help but be excited.

Ryusendo draft beer will be available from July! In the future, the attached brewery and taproom will be brewing craft beers that can only be had here, such as wild grapes, apples, salt, and grains, using water from Ryusendo Cave, so be sure to try them! Sake from the local sake brewery “Izumikin Sake Brewery”, which won a gold medal at the National Sake Appraisal, was also on display, allowing us to once again appreciate the blessings of Iwaizumi Town’s water.

Ryusendo Cave is one of Japan’s three largest limestone caves and has been designated as a national natural monument. The fresh water gushing out from the depths forms underground lakes in several places, and the third underground lake is 98 meters deep and boasts one of the clearest waters in the world. The lake water, known as dragon blue, and the countless stalactites inside the cave will transport you to a fantastical world.

ViTO x IWAIZUMI is a combination of Italian authentic gelato brand ViTO and Iwate’s fresh raw milk and Iwaizumi yogurt. The showcase, which makes everyone cheer as soon as they see it, always has a lineup of 18 fascinating types!

I was confused, but I couldn’t pass up “Blue Dragon Salt”! The syrup is inspired by the dragon blue of Ryusendo Cave, and when served, it is mixed with milk-based gelato and transformed into a gentle pastel color. I ordered the triple cone (¥530) along with the premium one made with Iwaizumi’s strawberries and blueberries.
The standard product here is Iwaizumi Yogurt, which is well-known for its refreshing packaging.
Ryusendo Cave Carbonated Water, which was served at the G7 Hiroshima Summit in May of this year, is also an exciting product.

We found a cute cafe on the hill in Tanohata Village, inside the Takuyodai housing complex! The store has a bright atrium and a stylish gazebo in the well-kept garden. The “Spider Soda” (¥260), which has a moe-like visual that looks like a spiky cloud floating in a small ocean in a glass, and the “Watame Soft (¥370)”, which comes in 7 colors, will make you feel fluffy!

The name Kumo came from the owner’s mother who said, “Opening a cafe is like grabbing a cloud.” I started making cotton candy because I thought children would enjoy it, and it fit perfectly with the concept. There is also a wide variety of light meals on the menu, including “Carbonara (¥770)” with large cuts of bacon and hot sandwiches.

A sparkling sea and a chalk lighthouse. There was a world where Fudai Village’s catchphrase, “Land of Blue”, was exactly what it was! Rikuchu Kurosaki Lighthouse, which was certified as a “lighthouse in love” in 2019, is located on the 40th parallel north, the same as New York and Madrid. It is an active lighthouse that still watches over ships sailing at night from the top of a 130m high cliff, and it is also a sacred place of romance that illuminates the future of the couple who visit here.
I tried ringing the carillon bell, which is said to bring happiness. May your wishes for peace reach wherever you are, riding on the sacred sounds.
To commemorate the 10th anniversary of Ama-chan’s broadcast, a wrapped train made by fans is in operation.

This is a guesthouse where you can drink homemade Doburoku made at the Doburoku Factory. Ichi-no-Shizuku is made using Iwate prefecture-produced rice “Ginotome” and “Iwatekko,” and is characterized by its simple and gentle flavor, with a thick and smooth texture that brings out the flavor of the rice. Blended with ancient rice, you can enjoy the pink color and elegant taste of “Ichi-no-Shizuku (red)”. We also sell limited quantities to people who are not staying overnight.
“Ichi no Shizuku (red)” is a blend of homemade doburoku “Ichi no Shizuku (white)” and ancient rice.

This is a guesthouse where you can drink handmade doburoku. “Shiro no Shizuku,” which is carefully made from home-grown rice and spring water at the foot of Mt. Iwate, is smooth and easy to drink, while “Aka no Shizuku” is made from home-grown ancient rice and has a wine-like flavor.
Doburoku “Shiro no Shizuku” made with home-grown rice
Minshuku Sakaiso (Sakai Hisae)

“Yuki no Chikara” is built in Nishiwaga Town, which is located on the prefectural border of Iwate and Akita and is known as the area with the heaviest snowfall in Iwate Prefecture. Using Nishiwaga rice harvested in autumn as the raw material, high-quality groundwater from the Higusa River is used for brewing, and the rice is slowly fermented while keeping the temperature low to create a sweet flavor. Although the sugar content exceeds 15 degrees, it has a refreshing acidity and is easy to drink.The sweet taste of Doburoku makes it easy for women to drink and enjoy. Please enjoy it with delicious Nishiwaga ingredients. *This is a winter limited item.
Nishiwaga doburoku “Yuki no Chikara” and “Yuki no Chikara (dry)”
Nishiwaga Industrial Corporation Co., Ltd.

This is Doburoku from Tono City, the first Doburoku Special Zone in Japan. Doburoku, which was once brewed at home, is a regional flavor. Aiming for the taste of Doburoku that is loved by Miyamori in Tono City, we use the Iwate sake rice “Ginginga” grown by the Miyamori River Upstream Production Association, and the association handles everything from brewing to bottling. Doburoku is thick and has a gentle sweetness derived from rice, making it easy to pair with meals. On February 17, 2020, “New Rice Doburoku Sweet” won a prize at the “National Doburoku Research Competition” held in Obu City, Aichi Prefecture.
Tono Doburoku Amakuchi/Karakuchi
● Support period: All year round
● Visit hours: 10:30~ Closed on Saturdays, Sundays, Golden Week, and New Year’s holidays
● Time required: Approximately 30 minutes ● Capacity: Approximately 5 people
● Application: Advance application required via email miyamori-kakou@wit.ocn.ne.jp
Agricultural Cooperative Corporation Miyamori River Upstream Production Association Nigori Sake Manufacturing Plant

First doburoku special zone and first manufacturing license in Tono City. Doburoku at MILK-INN Egawa, a farm guesthouse located in the natural surroundings of Tono’s mountains and offering a variety of nature experiences, is the result of the owner’s desire for guests to enjoy local cuisine with the local atmosphere and alcohol. It was created from thought. There are three types of doburoku, which are made using “kakehashi” harvested from the rice fields in front of the guest house, and have a strong rice flavor. The first to be produced, Kaitaku, the slightly sweeter Gokoku, and the pink, Hana, are the sweetest. Enjoy the nostalgic flavors unique to this region.
Tono Doburoku Cultivation, Flowering, Grains

This Doburoku from Tono City is the first Doburoku Special Zone in Japan. It is made in the traditional way, without using any unnecessary ingredients, and uses Tono’s “Akitakomachi” as the main ingredient, and is finished with water from the Tono mountains, domestically produced rice malt, and yeast. It is produced in almost the same way as amazake, so although it is alcoholic, it contains the same rich nutrients as amazake. It’s sweet enough to make you ask, “Does it have sugar in it?” It’s just the sweetness of pure rice. There are easy-to-drink sweet varieties with low alcohol content and dry varieties with a refreshing taste. Enjoy the traditional flavor.
Hiraizumi’s Doburoku One Sound

Doburoku was started by five energetic farming mothers from Hiraizumi Town. We use only “Hitomebore” caught in the town, and the sweetness and rich, deep flavor are appealing. The name “One Sound” comes from the “Chusonji Temple Memorial Memorial”, which says, “May the single sound of this bell, which resounds equally throughout the world, lead the souls of those who have lost their lives to the Pure Land of Paradise.” It seems that this symbolic “one sound” was used as the name for Doburoku. “Koshiraku” is made using red yeast and has a beautiful pink color. Packed in a cute heart-shaped bottle, it is also recommended as a gift.
● Visit time: Consultation required
● Capacity: Approximately 5 people
● Application: Reservation required by phone

“Kanrakuro” is a farmhouse inn built in an old folk house that was built about 140 years ago. The owner manages the guest house, grows rice, makes doburoku, and maintains the flower garden all by himself. “Anchan’s Doburoku” made at the Doburoku workshop takes about three weeks to make using rice that they have grown themselves, and has a subtle sweetness and concentrated rice flavor. In addition to two types, sweet and dry, they also make “Jomon no Hana”, a sour wine-like doburoku made from the ancient rice “Asashi”. You can enjoy a nostalgic atmosphere when you sit around the hearth of an old folk house and enjoy it with your meal.

Enyama Sunflower Park (next to Enyama Park)

Sunflowers are planted in a 2 hectare field in the former Yanshan Nursery, located on the east side of the prefectural forestry technology center, next to Yanshan Forest Park. Every year, many people inquire about the sunflowers, and they are widely appreciated not only by people within the town but also by people from outside the town. It is also known by photography enthusiasts as a superb place to take pictures of a field of sunflowers with the Nanjosho Mountains in the background. For more information about the sunflower fields at Yakin Town's Wami Flower Park, please click here.

Shiwa Fruit Park is a winery that produces Shiwa's own wine, which is made with 100% grapes grown in Shiwa Town. There is a direct sales store where you can tour a wine factory and sample wines, a hands-on workshop where you can make pizza and soba noodles, and a hands-on farm where you can pick grapes.

La France Onsenkan boasts over 10 different types of Japanese and Western style baths, as well as open-air baths and saunas. The heated pool with a water slide that is 11m high and 86m long is very popular with children. For accommodation, please stay at Hotel Yurakuraku, which can host banquets and has a reputation for good food. You can play to your heart's content and relax.

This information dissemination base was named after the Morioka dialect for ``Please come.'' In addition to the `` Tourism and Culture Information Plaza '' on the second floor, there is also a shop selling specialty products and a light snack cafe. In addition, the `` Morioka Tegami Museum '' on the 6th floor stores and exhibits letters and diaries of great people connected to Morioka.
Nitobe Inazo’s birthplace (bronze statue)

To commemorate the 50th anniversary of the death of Inazo Nitobe, a cosmopolitan man born in his hometown who ``hopefully becomes a bridge over the Pacific Ocean'', Morioka City built this building on his birthplace in Shimonohashi Town with donations from citizens. Author Fumio Asakura). During the Pacific War, its achievements were largely ignored, and its legacy was only remembered by a few people, but after the war, its role was properly reviewed and reevaluated on both sides of the Pacific.

This is the communal well that Kenji Miyazawa used when he was a student at Morioka High School of Agriculture and Forestry (currently Iwate University Faculty of Agriculture) in 1912, when he was lodging with his younger brother Seiroku and cousin at the Tamai family in Osawagawara 1-chome. It is still freely available.
Morioka Castle Ruins Park (Iwate Park)

This is the former site of Morioka Castle, which was the residence of the lords of the Nanbu domain. Morioka Castle was completed in 1633 during the reign of Shigenao, the third lord of the domain. The castle was built on a hillside at the confluence of the former Kitakami River and Nakatsu River. Today, the stonewalls and pond remain, and the area is known as Morioka Castle Ruins Park, which is enjoyed by citizens throughout the four seasons.
Morioka History and Culture Museum

Formerly the Iwate Prefectural Library, the Morioka Museum of Art was completely renovated and opened in 2011 in a corner of Morioka Castle Ruins Park (Iwate Park), with the first floor introducing Morioka's festivals (Chagu Chagu Umako, Morioka Sansa Odori, Morioka Fall Festival floats) and seasonal tourist information, and the second floor displaying the history of the Morioka clan and treasures of the Nanbu family. Please stop by to experience the history and culture of the castle town of Morioka and enjoy walking around the town.

The bridge above was built by Toshinao, the lord of the Nanbu domain, over the Nakatsugawa River at the same time as he built Morioka Castle. Of the bronze imitation jewels decorating the railing, eight have inscriptions dated to 1609 (Keicho 14), and 10 have inscriptions dated to 1611 (1611). It is extremely rare that so many remain, and in 1945 it was designated as a nationally important art object.

The remains of the fire station, which was built in 1913 (Taisho 2) and is a Morioka city landscape important building. After undergoing earthquake-proofing and renovation work, it reopened as a new exchange experience facility in March 2022 (Reiwa 4). There is a cafe and miscellaneous goods sales on the first floor, and a weaving workshop on the second floor, where you can also experience it by making a reservation. You can relax in a restaurant that exudes Taisho romance.

It opened as Iwate Bank Red Brick Building on Sunday, July 17, 2016. Built to the design of Kingo Tatsuno and Manji Kasai Architects, the former Morioka Bank is built of red brick with a green dome, and its exterior has a strict Renaissance-style outline. Located in the center of the city, it combines with the Nakatsu River and Nakano Bridge to form Morioka's representative landscape. A nationally designated important cultural property built in 1909.
Morioka Takuboku/Kenji Seishunkan

The Morioka Takuboku and Kenji Youth Museum is located in the former Dai Kuju Bank, which was completed in 1908, and introduces the town of Morioka where Takuboku Ishikawa and Kenji Miyazawa grew up and their youth. Designated as a National Important Cultural Property on July 6, 2004

Morioka Hachimangu Shrine was built in 1680 by the 29th Lord Shigenobu Nanbu. The deity enshrined at Morioka Hachimangu Shrine is Shinada Wake no Mikoto (15th Emperor Ojin), who has been revered by local people since ancient times as the god of the roots of human life such as agriculture, industry, commerce, learning, food, clothing, and shelter. have been collected. Due to disasters such as the Great Morioka Fire in 1884 and damage from wind and snow over many years, the shrine building has been repeatedly rebuilt, and the current shrine building was rebuilt in December 1997. The vermilion-painted main shrine building with its colorful carvings exudes an imposing atmosphere as the new ``face of Morioka.'' As the largest shrine in the prefecture, and as a place of worship and celebrations that are rooted in people's lives, it is still crowded with visitors throughout the year.

The 21 stone statues that remain on the grounds of Souryuji Temple were built to commemorate the victims of the famine that occurred during the Nanbu domain era. It was started in 1837 and completed in 1849, thirteen years later. It took over half a year just to transport the rock from the neighboring town of Yahaba, where it was cut, to this location. In addition, the statues were carved by craftsmen employed by the domain, and stone statues made by local stonemasons are rare in Japan.

Daijiji Temple, also known as Hara Takashi's family temple, was built in 1673 with a rare Chinese-style temple gate. The hall was destroyed in a fire in 1899, but the Sanmon gate and the warehouse were rebuilt thanks to Takashi Hara's generosity.

A wealthy merchant family during the feudal period. Located in Somon, the gateway to the castle town of Morioka, it retains its original appearance and has a quaint earthen storehouse structure with fire prevention in mind. It was designated as a cultural property by Iwate Prefecture in 1981.

The family temple of Mitsumasa Yonai, the prime minister from Morioka. Founded during the Kanbun era (1661-1672). There is a neck mound that tells the legend of a lotus who stole the head of his executed father and offered it as a memorial service. It has been designated as a city-designated preservation building.

Gidaji and Daijiji are the water sources. It is built in a box shaped like a doll's platform, and from the top it is used for drinking water, rice polishing, washing water, and foot washing. It is still used by many people as daily water.

The sake brewery of the "Former Iwategawa Nataya-cho Factory", where sake was brewed until 2006, was renovated and opened as "Morioka Machiya Monogatari-kan". Of the four buildings, "Hamato's Sake Brewery" offers visitors a look at the history of the brewery and a video recording of the Showa period. In the "Gashiya" (the space under the eaves between the warehouses), visitors can view exhibits of valuable materials from the old Iwate River, and in the "Main House" there is a general information desk and community space where sightseeing information, art exhibitions, various lectures, and other events are held. The Taisho-gura, a sake brewery built in the Taisho era, has a "Toki-no Shotengai" on the first floor that sells Morioka's specialties and crafts, gelato, and a coffee shop, while the "Toki-no Exhibition Room" on the second floor is a gallery that regularly holds special exhibitions of art works from Morioka's collection.

You can see the process of making delicious local sake, which is unique to Morioka, a city with clean water, and learn about sake making. A guide will be available for tours of the facility, including the brewery (Showa Asahigura), product factory, and local sake product center.

據說它始於天正 15 年的志願者祈禱豐收和人民的健康，據說前往大阪冬令營營地的當地士兵在戰鬥間隙跳了七種祭品，受到了好評。 從那時起，它就從祖先傳給後代，現在該地區的許多年輕人都是保護協會的成員，並在各種活動中展示。 （工具：人們認為“七物”這個名字來自Senuchi、Yatsurai、Naginata、Kine、Tachi、Ogi和Okekatsugi的七種工具。 日期和時間：地區節日、活動等。
“千龍山”是宮古市唯一的清酒釀造公司Hishiya Sake Brewery的品牌名稱。 以三陸宮古引以為豪的凈多濱國立公園的風景名勝區為基礎，成立至今已有5年，擁有150年的悠久歷史，並繼續以南部森先生的技能和諧提供美味的清酒。 它因東日本大地震而遭到嚴重破壞，但最終已恢復。
這是一座非常古老且歷史悠久的神社，據說建於白鳳9年（681年）。 據說源義經的首席僕人參觀了朝聖並過夜。 據說他的附庸鈴木三郎重家年紀很大，所以他留在了橫山八宮神社，改名為十三郎，成為這個八幡宮的祭司。
據說，加光寺始於水與木從源朝的法名中取出寺廟的名字，並在根城建造了一座寺廟，以哀悼他的父親源朝源朝的去世。 起初是天臺宗，但後來在現在的位置建造了一座寺廟後，它變成了曹洞宗。 1792年，主幹道被大火燒毀，大正7年也著火了。 現在的正殿後來重建了。

The Iwate Prefecture coast, where the Oyashio and Kuroshio currents meet, is one of the world’s three major fishing grounds and a treasure trove of fresh seafood. In addition to the marine delicacies available in each area, the scenery sculpted by the unique geographical features of Sanriku, such as Kitayamazaki with its long stretch of 200-meter cliffs, Unosu Dangai (Cormorant’s Nest Cliffs), and the government-designated scenic spot of Jodogahama Beach, are simply breathtaking. The Hashino Iron Mine, a part of the World Heritage Site, Sites of Japan’s Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining, is located in this area.
Roadside Station “Tanohata” Wind of Thought

“Roadside Station Tanohata” was relocated and reopened in April 2021, 300 meters north of Shizuo Bridge. We carry a wide selection of products from Tanohata Village, which is blessed with the natural beauty of the sea, mountains, and land. There is also a fast food corner that uses plenty of ingredients from Tanohata Village, such as ``Tanohata Raw Milk Softsoft'' and ``Shiitake Frank,'' as well as a restaurant where ``Milk Noodles with Lots of Seaweed'' is popular. In addition, there is a quaint simple lodging facility "Shishisokan" in a renovated old folk house nearby, and there is also a parking lot for 5 campers, making it a new base as a "roadside station where you can stay overnight." .

A typical view of the ria coastline unfolds. Part of the rock has caved in, creating a narrow channel between the sheer cliffs, which is eroded by the waves of the Pacific Ocean. Waves change the topography over many years. You can catch a glimpse of nature's creation. The nearby garden is a hidden spot for camellias.

The Whale and Sea Science Museum aims to introduce the mysterious ocean from various angles and deepen visitors' interest in the ocean. Exhibits are organized by theme from the top of the building to the bottom, and you can explore it as if you were taking a walk into the ocean. The museum introduces the romantic world of whales through exhibits such as the world's largest skeletal specimen of a gigantic sperm whale, a creature of the sea.
Ryusendo Cave Hot Spring Hotel

Located at the foot of Mt. Urira, about a 10-minute walk from Ryusendo Cave, you can enjoy Kaiseki cuisine featuring Iwaizumi Tankaku beef, seasonal wild vegetables, and seafood. As a family bath, there is a charcoal bath that uses 400 kg of Bincho charcoal. It is popular for its far infrared rays and negative ion effects. The spring quality is slightly alkaline, and it is effective for treating neuralgia, skin diseases, and joint pain.
Sano Rock (prefecturally designated natural monument)

Sano-iwa, which appears to rise from the sea, is made up of three gigantic rocks: the drum-shaped Taiko-iwa, the 50m-high Otoko-iwa, and the Onna-iwa nearby. There is a sea cave in Otokowa, and it is said that passing through it will bring you good luck. The rock has layers of Cretaceous conglomerate and sandstone. There is a promenade nearby, and you can also do sea fishing. The further down the promenade you go, the closer you will see the brave rock formations. Dynamic rock fishing can be enjoyed all along the coast from Taro Port to Masaki and Myojinzaki. You can catch greenling, sea bass, donko, perch, mackerel, etc. The season is from May to December.

The birthplace of Haruyo Tottori (real name Kanichi), an enka performer and composer from the Taisho and early Showa eras, who was born in Kariya, the former Shinsato village in 1899, and died at the young age of 31, still exists. Haruyo Tottori moved to Tokyo at the age of 14 and began composing music at the age of 17, and his ``Caged Bird'', which he composed in 1923, became an unprecedented hit. She became Japan's first singer exclusively for a record company.
Kitayamazaki Cliff Cruise Tourist Boat

You can enjoy the impressive view of Kitayamazaki, a scenic spot representing Sanriku Fukko National Park, from the ocean. Flights depart from and arrive at Shimagoshi Port, located south of Kitayamazaki. There are waves to go out into the open ocean, but these are also very impressive. One lap is 50 minutes. Umineko bread is also sold on the cruise, and you can also experience feeding the sea cats.

Originally the general office of Kamaishi Mining Co., Ltd. Nationally registered tangible cultural property. It is also the largest iron mine in Japan and one of the leading copper mines in Japan. This is a facility that widely promotes Kamaishi Mine. It's perfect for learning about history and geology, with a floor that recreates the Kamaishi Mining School and mining office, and an exhibition corner of ore from the mines.
